newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kyushu Electric halves output at Genkai plant.
newsitem.headline: Kyushu Electric halves output at Genkai plant.

text.p: Kyushu Electric Power Co. on Saturday halved the power output at No. 1 reactor at its Genkai nuclear power plant in southwestern Japan after problems with a water condenser, the company said.
The power cutback was made following a warning signal showing that sea water had contaminated water in one of two condensers at the plant in Saga prefecture, the firm said.
The company identified cracks in a pipe within the condenser as a likely cause of the sea water seepage, but added it would take several days to locate the cracks.
There was no danger of radiation emissions, the firm said.
Kyushu Electric Power on Tuesday announced it was bowing to local opposition and shelving plans to build another nuclear power plant in southern Kyushu, the southernmost of Japan's four main islands.

The problems at the Genkai plant follow the nation's worst radiation leak, in which a fire and explosion on Tuesday at Tokaimura nuclear power plant, 160 km (100 miles) northeast of Tokyo, exposed 37 workers to radiation and may have cause trace amounts of plutonium to leak into the air.
